# Direct cap budgets remove the cap-quantile smoothness assumption

The stable planar support-arc and positive-curvature hypotheses of
candidate 2d6d202be366ee4e remain in Sections1--5 below. Selected
caps may now coincide with fiber facets anywhere away from that arc. No C2
cap quantile is used.

## 1. A finite exact cover and an explicitly feasible acceleration cone

Fix an attained local depth minimum with positive finite fibers, total area
M, and beta>0. Put D=beta M. Select one critical circuit at each deepest
fiber, and keep a slack whole-fiber circuit at every nondeep fiber. Every
critical cap has mass D. The continuous circuit normals u_j are nonzero;
normalize them at the base if desired. Write each cap as

    u_j.x+v_j.z>=b_j.

Use fixed positive circuit coefficients rho. Cap accelerations (du,dv,db)
obey the exact linear whole-fiber-cover conditions

    sum_j rho_j du_j=0,
    sum_j rho_j(dv_j.z-db_j)>=0

at its assigned fiber z. For a more general fixed assignment, impose these
derivative inequalities ONLY where the original covering margin is zero;
strictly positive margins persist without a sign condition on their
derivatives. Otherwise the negative joint homothety could be excluded
unnecessarily. They preserve the closed cover
at parameter size epsilon, since the original weighted margins are zero
and their changes are linear in epsilon. Slack groups can remain fixed.

Body accelerations consist of signed compatible support changes psi on the
stable arc and one signed common continuous homothety kappa. They are
realized by first changing support functions on the arc, then multiplying
all continuous fibers by 1+epsilon*kappa. This preserves compatibility;
the compact arc changes preserve its fixed equalities and strict remaining
gaps. Outside the arc nothing changes except the common homothety.

Only finitely many arc acceleration coordinates are needed. Every first
objective/cap derivative from psi depends on it through the vector

    U_z(psi)=integral psi_z dr_z.

The image of the compatible arc test space under U is finite-dimensional;
choose any finite basis of that image and one admissible preimage for each
basis vector. This retains ALL its first-order mass information. The full
acceleration cone A is now a closed polyhedral cone: its body coordinates
and kappa are free, and the cap coordinates satisfy the displayed linear
equalities and inequalities.

Its objective derivative is the single linear functional

    L0(a)=2 kappa M+sum_z U_z(psi).                          (1)

## 2. Compact consistent cap-gradient sets, including boundary facets

For each critical cap j construct the following compact convex set Gj of
linear functionals of the SAME acceleration coordinates. After pulling the
common homothety back to the original body, the affine relative margin on
the old cap plane is

    ell_j(z,x)=du_j.x+kappa u_j.x+dv_j.z-db_j.

The gradient contains the fixed terms

    2 kappa D+sum_z I_jz U_z(psi),

where I_jz is the cap's constant strict membership on the affected arc.
Add the integral of ell_j/|u_j| on every ordinary proper fiber section.
For a coincident supporting fiber facet F, add instead

    integral_F theta(z,x) ell_j(z,x)/|u_j| dH1,
    0<=theta(z,x)<=1.                                      (2)

The SAME measurable theta in (2) determines its mass, integer-coordinate,
and continuous first-moment coefficients. These coefficients must not be
chosen independently. The set of their joint finite-dimensional moments
is compact and convex (bounded densities on a finite measure space are
weak-star compact, and the finitely many moment maps are continuous).
Independent fiber faces may have independent subdensities.

The actual one-sided cap derivative Dj(a) belongs to Gj evaluated at a:
at an inside supporting coincidence the local term is min(ell_j,0)/|u_j|,
and at an outside supporting coincidence it is max(ell_j,0)/|u_j|.
Choose theta pointwise as the relevant sign indicator. Proper sections use
the ordinary coarea derivative; zero-length tangent faces contribute zero.
These statements also follow directly by integrating the swept strips
normal to the cap line and applying dominated convergence. Consequently

    Dj(a) <= sup_(g in Gj) g(a).                             (3)

No differentiability at a coincident face is being assumed.

The two signed JOINT homotheties are particularly important. Take kappa=1,
psi=0, du_j=0, dv_j=v_j, db_j=b_j, and its negative. On every old section
ell_j=u_j.x+v_j.z-b_j=0. Hence EVERY g in Gj agrees on these directions:

    L0(a_h)=2M,       g(a_h)=2D.                             (4)

Both directions lie in A, and the equalities hold even at coincidences.

## 3. Conic second-order mass vectors and actual improving paths

Let L be the common kernel of the active support compatibility equalities
on the stable arc. The disjoint-bump construction in the preceding note
realizes every finite conic sum of the vectors

    B0(v)=-sum_z v_z^2,
    Bj(v)=-sum_z I_jz v_z^2,           v in L.                (5)

All first objective and cap masses vanish for these bump perturbations.
Let B=(B0,Bj) be any such finite conic sum, represented by a first-order
support perturbation delta h. Combine it with acceleration a at size
epsilon=t^2/2. The actual feasible path is obtained by arc support changes
t delta h+epsilon psi, common homothety1+epsilon kappa, and the indicated
cap motions at size epsilon.

The resulting expansions are

    M(t)=M+epsilon[B0+L0(a)]+o(t^2),
    mu_t(H_j(t))=D+epsilon[Bj+Dj(a)]+o(t^2).                 (6)

There is no hidden smooth-quantile interchange here. The first-order arc
changes have a strict gap from every cap plane, so all actual cap sections
and all coincident facets remain untouched by those changes. Their mass
contribution is exactly the constant-indicator area change. The order-t^2
cap/homothety motion elsewhere has the one-sided derivative just computed.
Cross terms are o(t^2). Convexity and compatibility hold by the explicit
construction, and the cover constraints hold exactly.

It follows that a pair (B,a) satisfying

    B0+L0(a)>0,
    Bj+sup_(g in Gj)g(a)<0         for every critical j       (7)

would contradict local minimality. The total area would increase while
every critical cap stayed below the original absolute budget D; slack caps
remain slack. The fixed exact closed cover would then bound the new depth
strictly below D/M=beta.

## 4. Robust epigraph separation and normalization

Let Bcone be the convex cone generated by (5), and form the convex cone E
of all vectors (x0,xj) for which there exist B in Bcone and a in A with

    x0<=B0+L0(a),
    xj>=Bj+sup_(g in Gj)g(a).

Convexity follows from the support-function inequality for each compact
convex Gj. By (7), E is disjoint from the OPEN convex cone

    O={x0>0 and every xj<0}.

Separation gives coefficients alpha0>=0, lambda_j>=0, not all zero, with

    -alpha0 x0+sum_j lambda_j xj >=0       on E.

Cone closure is unnecessary because O is open. The freely downward x0 and
upward xj coordinates give the stated coefficient signs. Setting a=0 and
using (5) yields

    alpha0 sum_z v_z^2-sum_jz lambda_j I_jz v_z^2>=0
                                      for every v in L.     (8)

Setting B=0 gives for every a in A

    -alpha0 L0(a)+sum_j lambda_j sup_(g in Gj)g(a)>=0.        (9)

Evaluate (9) on BOTH directions in (4). It follows that

    alpha0 M=D sum_j lambda_j.

If alpha0 were zero, every lambda_j would be zero, contradicting nonzero
separation. Thus alpha0>0. Divide all coefficients by alpha0. We obtain

    sum_j lambda_j=1/beta,
    sum_z W_z v_z^2>=0 for every v in L,
    W_z=1-sum_j lambda_j I_jz.                              (10)

The normalization uses a concrete exact two-sided path; no unproved
constraint qualification or positive objective coefficient is assumed.

## 5. The same stress controls first variations

On arc-supported accelerations every allowed gradient in Gj agrees, since
the changed boundary region has strict fixed cap membership. Such motions
occur in both signs in A. Therefore (9) gives equality on all of them:

    sum_z W_z integral psi_z dr_z=0.                         (11)

The finite basis chosen in Section1 retains the feature vector of every
admissible arc test, so (11) holds for all those tests. In the smooth
positive-curvature setting, put psi_z=v_z phi for arbitrary compact smooth
phi and v in L. Then

    sum_z W_z r_z(theta)v_z=0 for every theta in I, v in L.

Together with r(theta) in L and (10), this puts the curvature vector in the
fixed nullspace of the positive-semidefinite diagonal form on L.

If cap-coordinate stress equations are also needed, one can choose ONE
consistent gradient from each Gj. Indeed, let G=sum_j lambda_j Gj, compact
and convex. Equation (9) says sup_(g in G)(g-L0)(a)>=0 for every a in A.
If G were disjoint from L0+A*, where A* is the closed dual cone of A,
strict separation of the compact set from that closed convex set would
give a in A with sup_(g in G)(g-L0)(a)<0, a contradiction. Thus choose
g_j in Gj with sum_j lambda_j g_j-L0 in A*. This choice retains the joint
measurable trace moments of Section2. It is not obtained by independently
choosing convenient section masses and centroids.

The result removes the selected-cap C2 assumption. Its remaining geometric
limitations are the stable compatibility/gap arc and the availability of
the signed curvature perturbations. It does not itself prove that an
arbitrary minimizer admits a global finite arc decomposition.
